jk_m1.line: Oh, that's me, that's a mic, don't touch it, it's fine, I also have the plumber's on a loop and I've been using the Reverend for rhythm. You've seen the tabulating machine they put in at the insurance? Instructions for waking, working, eating and sleeping. Left out the part where a person gets to be alive. I'm recording that part. Somebody should.

choices.label: Who else knows it's up there?

jk_m2.line: Sacha, Thursdays, because Thursdays are Sacha's and we fight about it. Adela Voss told me my cable was in her shot and moved it. Nicely! Moved it nicely! And she never told a soul. I'd have told a soul.

jk_m3.line: ... No. That's a real question, you're allowed that one. No.

jk_w1.line: I have the tape. We don't have to play it now.

jk_w2.line: Okay. It's on the shelf where you left it. It's on the shelf, I mean. I don't know why I said that.

jk_w3.line: Lights died, deck kept going, I'd rigged it off a cell because I'm like that. Thump of the house going off. Then rain. Then some hours of rain. Nobody on it. It's the best rain I ever got. I'm sorry, that's what I think, I don't have another thing to think.

jk_t1.line: "Saturday the twenty-fourth, three p.m., C.D., WLBQ twelfth and nineteenth July." We swap air. He gets my cold splices and I get his night dial. Lena through the wall is the only audience we've got, I tell her a joke: nothing. I slam the cupboard: hysterics. There's something wrong with the profession.

jk_t2.line: He says somebody's clock was in both and he hates it. Go ask him, bring a chair, he'll play it till you agree with him.

jk_p1.line: Oh, that's me, that's on, that's four-eleven of the Harukiya with people in it, it's not a crime it's a Saturday. There's a man in Elmhurst being summoned for selling a room, but I'm not selling, I'm only keeping it where nobody can get at it. Adela wants to mail it to Astoria. Miss Sato wants me dead. They've both been up here.

jk_p2.line: That's what the shouting is. That's the asking. It's going very well.

jk_d1.line: I cut it. She stood on my rug with her arms folded and I cut it and she took it down to the ashcan herself. That's true, you can check that, that's the whole truth about that reel.

jk_d1s.line: Good. That's all, then. That's all.

jk_d2.line: I dubbed that one. It was good, so I dubbed it, the day before she came up. So there's a second one. I haven't played it since. That's a lie, I've played it. I don't know why I'm telling the man who does the radiators.

jk_d2s.line: Yeah. It's in the box with the others. It's got a label, I don't do labels, it's got a label.

jk_d3.speaker: THE REEL
jk_d3.line: (Four minutes and eleven seconds of a Saturday in May. A woman is singing who has never once heard this from out here. She is a little flat in the second chorus and she does not care. Near the finish the whole room comes in early, right over something she had planned, and another voice comes in underneath, and breaks, and goes on.)

jk_d5.line: Oh, now the radiators have a view.

jk_d4.line: ... No. I'll ask. I said I'll ask. It's the only reel with that woman's left hand on it and I'd like that noted. I don't know who by.

choices.label: She's flat in the second chorus.

jk_g1.line: It's cut. Miss Sato came up and stood on the same rug. I cut it, and I didn't dub it. You can check that. You can't check that. I didn't.
